title: Beach Volleyball Tournament Poster
description: A graphic design project exploring typography, colour theory, and visual hierarchy through the creation of a promotional poster for a fictional volleyball tournament in the Town of Shelbyville. Every element was constructed entirely within Adobe Illustrator, demonstrating vector illustration skills and intentional compositional decisions.

title: Furrever Pals Puppy Yoga
description: A branding and UI/UX project for a fictional puppy yoga studio designed to address mental health and community connection in Vancouver. The project spans brand identity, visual system design, and service design with every asset created in Figma and Adobe Creative Suite. The goal was to build a brand that feels as welcoming and purposeful as the service it represents.

title: MyBCIT Page Re-Design
description: A full UI/UX redesign of MyBCIT, BCIT's student portal. Through user research, iterative prototyping, and usability testing with over ten participants, the project proposes a redesigned interface that reduces navigation complexity, lowers the learning curve for new students, and modernises the visual system while staying true to BCIT's established brand identity.

title: Boardwalk Boutique App Design
description: A mobile app concept developed using the Waterfall methodology for a project management intensive. Working within a group, I led the UI design for a skateboard and streetwear rental and retail platform. The app allows users to browse inventory, book rentals, receive notifications, and locate the physical store, combining e-commerce and service design into a single cohesive experience.

title: Bing: The Redesign
description: A collaborative UI redesign of the Bing search engine focused on reducing visual clutter and improving navigational clarity. Working alongside a team of designers, the project streamlined the interface to surface the most relevant features and help users find what they need more efficiently without the cognitive overhead of the original layout.

title: National Geographics Magazine Design
description: A Photoshop composition exploring the intersection of imagination and reality through deliberate photo manipulation, layering, and visual storytelling. The iconic National Geographic format served as a canvas to examine the boundaries between the natural world and creative interpretation.
